Beyond the obvious · twice-weekly edit

Unusual London events,
this week.

Discover free and affordable things to do in London this week and weekend, selected for unusual access, local character and a story worth following. Every listing is checked against the official organiser before publication.

Friday 25 September – Sunday 27 September · Last edited 24 September at 15:01

Friday 25 September, 00:00 – Sunday 27 September, 23:59

Gift to the Future at Southbank Centre

More than 90 lines written with thousands of school pupils turn the Southbank Centre’s brutalist exterior into a site-wide poetry installation inspired by the 1951 Festival of Britain.

Venue
Southbank Centre, Riverside Terrace
Address
Belvedere Road, London, SE1 8XX
Access
Drop in

Sacred Treasures from Kyiv at the V&A

Seven Ukrainian Baroque sacred works from the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra are shown in the UK for the first time, including an icon, altar Gospel and silver chalice.

Venue
V&A South Kensington
Address
Cromwell Road, London, SW7 2RL

Friday 25 September, 10:00 – Sunday 27 September, 18:00

Amar Kanwar at Serpentine North

A darkened, site-specific environment brings together lyrical films on decolonisation, displacement and Partition, including the premiere of the seven-screen work The Charcoal Man.

Venue
Serpentine North Gallery
Address
West Carriage Drive, Kensington Gardens, London, W2 2AR
Access
Booking recommended

Japanese Women Photographers: From 1950s to Now

The final weekend brings together more than 200 photographs, videos, installations and rare books by 27 women whose work challenges a male-dominated account of Japanese photography.

Venue
The Photographers’ Gallery
Address
16-18 Ramillies Street, London, W1F 7LW

Drawn into Your Presence in Clapham

A local photographer pairs 30 enlarged Victorian Bible engravings with 30 contemporary images of south London church life inside a Grade II-listed post-war church.

St James’ Church, Clapham

Reviving Craft at Somerset House

More than 70 artists trace China’s living craft heritage through ceramics, glass, textiles, jewellery, furniture and immersive digital work in the South Wing galleries.

Woolmen Sheep Drive and Livery Fair

Freemen revive their ancient right to drive sheep over the Thames while the public explores livery trades, wool crafts, blade shearing and rare breeds beside Southwark Bridge.

Venue

Harvest Festival at Brixton Windmill

Inner London’s only working windmill celebrates the wheat harvest with milling demonstrations, baking and craft workshops, hand querns, Morris dancing and local live music.
